title: Can You Retake MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment?
summary: Learn how retaking MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment works, how grades and boundaries are applied, and what students and coordinators must arrange.
body_markdown:
Yes, **retaking MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment** is generally possible. A student can sit the on-screen examination in a later session to improve an existing result or help meet the requirements for the IB MYP Certificate.


However, students cannot register independently. An authorized IB World School must complete the registration, and the examination must be available in the intended session. The first step is therefore to contact the school's MYP coordinator.


### Official rules on MYP eAssessment retakes


The current[MYP general regulations](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/become-an-ib-school/pdfs/myp-2026-general-regulations.pdf) recognize an **extended period of study when a student retakes one or more subjects** . Completing MYP Year 5 does not prevent a student from returning for a later eAssessment.


The IB also removed the former **three-session rule** in 2023 for the MYP, Diploma Programme, and Career-related Programme. Older documents may still claim that candidates have only three sessions to obtain the MYP Certificate, but that is no longer the programme-wide rule.


This does not guarantee unlimited attempts. Each retake still depends on:


- registration through an authorized school
- examination availability in the intended session
- registration deadlines and fees
- current IB assessment procedures
- the school's willingness and capacity to administer the examination


A retake may be useful after a lower-than-expected grade, a result below **grade 3** , an absence that produced no usable result, or when a stronger mathematics grade is needed for a later academic pathway. It is different from a classroom reassessment because the eAssessment is an externally marked IB examination.


### Registration and examination sessions


The school where the original examination was taken is normally the best first contact. Its coordinator must confirm whether the school will register the candidate, offer Extended Mathematics in the required session, and administer the examination in an available response language.


The public IB[MYP registration timetable](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/onscreen-examinations/registration/) lists **20 October** as the registration deadline for a May session and **20 April** for a November session. Schools usually set earlier internal deadlines to collect candidate details, fees, and identification information.


Students should contact the coordinator several months in advance. A place is not automatic, and the coordinator must check current subject availability and procedures through IB systems before confirming the registration.


### How MYP Extended Mathematics is assessed


Extended Mathematics is assessed through an externally marked on-screen examination. The official[MYP mathematics assessment overview](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief-mathematics-en.pdf) identifies three broad task types connected to the four mathematics criteria.


Examination task Main focus Criteria emphasized


Knowing and understanding Selecting and applying mathematical knowledge **A and C**


Investigating patterns Generalizing, testing, and justifying relationships **B and C**


Applying mathematics in real-life contexts Modelling, interpreting, and evaluating results **C and D**


The criteria are **A: Knowing and understanding** , **B: Investigating patterns** , **C: Communicating** , and **D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts** . Criterion C appears throughout because notation, logical working, graphs, units, and mathematical language influence many responses.


Students should not apply the familiar classroom total out of 32 to the external examination. In school-based assessment, teachers award achievement levels from 0 to 8 across four criteria. The eAssessment instead produces externally awarded marks that the IB converts into a final subject grade.


### MYP Extended Mathematics grade boundaries


The final result is reported on the **1 to 7 scale** . The IB establishes subject-specific grade boundaries for each examination session by comparing candidate work with the relevant grade descriptors.


This means:


1. **A raw mark is not the final grade.** It must be compared with the official boundary table for that session.
2. **Boundaries can change.** The same raw mark is not guaranteed to produce the same grade in different sessions.
3. **Classroom boundaries out of 32 do not apply.** Those ranges concern criterion-level school assessment, not external examination marks.


Future boundaries cannot be known with certainty before the examination has been marked and the grade-awarding process completed. Any boundary used during revision is therefore only an estimate.


### Hypothetical grading example


These figures demonstrate the process and are not official boundaries.


Stage Example


Original Extended Mathematics grade 3


Retake raw mark 67


Hypothetical grade 5 range 65--74


New subject grade 5


Original certificate total 29 points


Revised certificate total 31 points


Here, the raw mark of 67 falls within the hypothetical grade 5 range. The reported result is therefore grade 5, not a percentage grade of 67%.


The[IB's grading and awards guidance](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/grading-and-awards/) states that the highest available applicable grade contributes to the relevant certificate requirement. Replacing grade 3 with grade 5 would raise the example total from 29 to 31.


The MYP Certificate has a maximum of **56 points** , based on eight required results worth up to seven points each. A candidate must obtain at least **28 points overall** , achieve at least **grade 3 in every required component** , and meet the school's service expectations. A higher mathematics grade can improve the total, but it cannot compensate for another required component that remains below grade 3.


### Can a lower retake result reduce the certificate total?


For the relevant certificate requirement, the **highest available grade** contributes when a student has completed more than one applicable eAssessment. A lower retake result should therefore not replace a higher original grade in the certificate calculation.


The student's assessment history and certificate calculation are not necessarily identical records. The coordinator should explain how results from different sessions will appear on official documentation.


Changing from Extended Mathematics to Mathematics is also not necessarily treated as a straightforward retake. The coordinator must verify current registration rules and how the result would meet the mathematics subject-group requirement. A candidate cannot take Mathematics and Extended Mathematics in the same examination session.


### Retake or enquiry upon results?


A disappointing result does not automatically make a retake the best option. Students should first review the available result information with their teacher and ask the coordinator about permitted post-results services.


An enquiry reviews an existing result, while a retake creates a new result after another examination. A retake is usually more appropriate when weaknesses exist in content knowledge, reasoning, communication, application, or timing. An enquiry may be worth discussing when a result is unexpectedly close to the next boundary, although deadlines, fees, and possible outcomes must be confirmed by the coordinator.


### Preparing for the retake


Effective preparation begins with diagnosis rather than repeating general revision. Students should classify mistakes under the four criteria and use that analysis to set priorities.


A focused plan should include:


- **Criterion A:** rebuild weak skills in algebra, functions, geometry, trigonometry, statistics, and probability
- **Criterion B:** practise identifying patterns, forming general rules, and justifying conclusions
- **Criterion C:** show complete working, use accurate notation, label graphs, and organize reasoning clearly
- **Criterion D:** select suitable models, interpret answers in context, use units, and evaluate limitations
- **Digital technique:** practise entering expressions and navigating multi-part on-screen tasks
- **Timed performance:** complete extended sets without pausing to consult notes


The[RevisionDojo MYP Extended Mathematics hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics) can organize content review. Students can use the[Extended Mathematics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics/questionbank) for targeted practice and the[topic lessons](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics/learn) to rebuild unfamiliar concepts.


The[30-day MYP eAssessment study plan](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-eassessments-30-day-study-plan) provides a structure for review, timed practice, and error analysis. The guide to[how MYP Mathematics is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) can help connect revision more directly to the criteria.


### Conclusion


Retaking MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment is possible, but an authorized IB World School must arrange it under the current registration and session requirements. The examination is externally marked, converted to a 1--7 grade using session-specific boundaries, and the highest applicable grade contributes to the certificate requirement.


Students should contact their coordinator early and prepare across all four criteria. RevisionDojo's Questionbank, lessons, Study Notes, timed practice, and Jojo AI can support a focused plan once registration is confirmed.
